q: Can a Delhi business buy green power from its discom?
title: Green power options for Delhi businesses
short: Only if DERC has set a green tariff for your category. The national Green Energy Open Access Rules, 2022 let any consumer ask its discom for renewable power at a green tariff fixed by the state commission. Ask BSES Rajdhani, BSES Yamuna, Tata Power-DDL or NDMC whether one is in force for you, and get the terms in writing.
audience: Delhi offices, hotels and small units on BSES or Tata Power-DDL supply

ol: Is a green tariff in force for my tariff category under the current DERC order, and what is the premium per kWh?
Can I cover a share of my consumption or must I cover all of it, and for what minimum period?
How will the green units appear on my bill?
Will you give me a yearly statement or certificate for the green units, confirming their attributes are not sold or claimed by anyone else?

sections.h: If no green tariff is on offer
ul: Green energy open access from a generator, if your load is 100 kW or more. Read DERC's current open access regulations for the connection and metering conditions that apply in Delhi before you approach developers.
Renewable energy certificates bought on a power exchange and retired for your units, which suit offices and hotels with no roof.
Rooftop solar under net metering, where you own or control the roof.

sections.h: Which option a buyer or guest will accept
p: Hotel groups and multinational tenants often report to group standards that name the instruments they accept. Before you pay a premium, ask whether a discom green tariff, Indian RECs or open access power is accepted, and what document they want each year.

sections.h: What it does to your Scope 2
p: Location-based Scope 2 is unchanged by any of these: all units consumed times the grid factor. Market-based Scope 2 falls only for units covered by a document that conveys the renewable attribute to you for your reporting period.

senseible: Senseible reads your BSES, Tata Power-DDL or NDMC bill for billing period, tariff category, sanctioned load and units, and reports location-based Scope 2 at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh (CEA, version 21.0). It reports market-based Scope 2 alongside when you record the green units or retired RECs with their certificate.
